BL-054.design:
**Status:** design-owed — shape settled 2026-07-08, the full design still owed; parked/out-of-scope, not promote-ready. Settling the structure now (per BL-087's model) so it's ready to pick up once nations move from generation-only to a system.

**Shape.** Four coupled parts, all deterministic and tick-driven like the rest of `world/*`:

1. **Nation SYSTEM.** A nation gets simple per-tick economic state — tax rate (levied on corp production/trade within its territory), a licence gate (a corp needs a licence to build/operate in a nation, cost scales with nation character), and a coarse infrastructure scalar (modulates production/logistics efficiency, generated once, degrading/improving slowly). War is a state flag between nation pairs affecting licence issuance and infrastructure decay, not a combat system — actual Conflict mechanics live elsewhere.
2. **Sentiment graph.** A small per-nation-pair scalar (-1..1) seeded at generation from shared borders/resource competition, drifting slowly from corp activity (heavy extraction in a nation nudges its sentiment toward the extracting corp's home nation). Read-only input to licence cost/availability; no diplomacy UI for the prototype's follow-on scope.
3. **Historical fragmentation.** Exclaves and disputed zones are a **generation-time** decoration on top of BL-053's Voronoi/merge output — after merge, some tiles are deliberately left owned by a non-contiguous or disputed neighbour rather than reassigned, for flavour and to justify uneven licence friction. Not a simulated historical event log.
4. **Non-Kepler jurisdiction.** Off-Earth bodies (once Era 1 opens them) start with no nation ownership — jurisdiction there is corp-claim-based, not nation-based; this item only needs to state that boundary, not design the space-claim system (that's Era 1 scope, BL-087-adjacent).

**Explicitly out of shape (defer further):** exact tax/licence formulas, sentiment decay/drift constants, war trigger conditions, the space-claim model. Those are sub-decisions for when this item is actually promoted, not now.

Authority docs/generation/NATION_GENERATION.md. Companion to BL-053 (which this builds on) and BL-087 (Era 1, for the non-Kepler boundary).

BL-230.design:
Ben (2026-07-30): "make sure tooltips do not stick when initially open, and take 1/2 a second before they appear, then 2 seconds before they stick. From cursor pov they are behind tiles until they stick, but from a rendering pov they are always in front."

**Landed.** Splits BL-228's single freeze-on-summon hover card into two phases: a GLANCE (kHoverAppearDelay = 30 frames @ 60 Hz = 0.5 s) that tracks the live cursor like an ordinary tooltip, then a STUCK freeze (kHoverStickDelay = 150 frames total = 2.5 s, i.e. 2 s after appearing) that stops tracking and is dismissed only once the pointer leaves its bounds + the existing exit pad. The window keeps ImGuiWindowFlags_NoInputs and the Tooltip flag throughout both phases, so it always draws above every other window (rendering pov) but never captures the pointer (cursor pov) — canvas hover/click always resolves to whatever tile or marker is beneath it, in either phase; nothing new was needed here since NoInputs already gave that property.

scripts/verify/hover_freeze.lua rewritten from 3 to 5 captures to exercise both phases (glance-appears, glance-tracks-cursor, stuck, pinned-after-nudge-while-stuck, dismissed-on-exit); goldens re-blessed.

BL-287.design:
MEASURED, NOT SUSPECTED (2026-08-04). A full verify-tier rebuild was taking 45-90 minutes and
blocking a session. The cause is one line: CMakeLists.txt:433

    add_executable(${harness_name} "${harness_src}" ${IO_WORLD_SOURCES})

Every harness target compiles the ENTIRE world layer from source. With 44 harnesses in
tools/verify/ and 30 world TUs in IO_WORLD_SOURCES, that is 1,320 compilations of the same 30
files per clean build. The object files are byte-identical across all 44 targets; only the
harness TU differs.

THE FIX. Compile the world layer once as an OBJECT library and link every harness against it:

    add_library(io_world_obj OBJECT ${IO_WORLD_SOURCES})
    target_include_directories(io_world_obj PUBLIC src)
    # per harness:
    add_executable(${harness_name} "${harness_src}" $<TARGET_OBJECTS:io_world_obj>)

That takes the world-layer compilation count from 1,320 to 30 — a 44x reduction on the
dominant cost. Harness TUs (44) stay as they are. Nothing about the harnesses themselves
changes; this is purely how the same objects are produced.

SECOND, SMALLER WIN. target_precompile_headers is applied only to ProjectIo (CMakeLists.txt:153),
so the harness tier — which is the overwhelming majority of the compiling — gets no PCH benefit.
The OBJECT library is the natural place to attach one.

ADJACENT, NOT PART OF THIS ITEM. The default build/ directory is configured NMake Makefiles +
Debug, which is single-threaded (15 of 16 cores idle) and produces harnesses that run ~30x
slower than Release. A build_rel/ directory already exists configured Ninja + Release and is
simply not the default anyone reaches for. Worth a line in DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES pointing at
it; that is documentation, not this code change.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING. This is not a micro-optimisation: it is the difference between a
verify-tier rebuild being a coffee break and being a session-ending event. Any change to a
widely-included header (components.hpp, world.hpp) currently invalidates all 1,320. The
BL-286 resource_type extension did exactly that and cost this session most of an hour.

VERIFICATION. Time a clean build of the verify tier before and after, and confirm ctest still
passes the same set. The object-library form must produce identical binaries — if any harness
behaves differently, something was depending on per-target compile flags and that is the real
finding.
BL-287.resolution:
LANDED 2026-08-04. src/world/*.cpp (minus the three Lua TUs) is now the OBJECT library
io_world_obj, compiled once. The 44-harness foreach and both Lua harnesses
(pregame_balance, persona_counsel) link it instead of listing ${IO_WORLD_SOURCES} as their
own sources. Include dir and cxx_std_20 are PUBLIC so consumers inherit them by linking;
IO_WARNING_FLAGS stays PRIVATE so it applies to the world layer and does not leak onto a
consumer's TU. World-layer compilations per clean build: 1,320 -> 30.

Full-tier incremental rebuilds now run in 1.5-6.5 s. A true from-cold number was NOT
measured: a fresh configure currently fails downloading SDL3 (see NR-048), so verification
reused build_rel, whose deps are cached.

IT ALSO EXPOSED A LATENT CRASH, which is exactly what this item said to watch for. Changing
link order made econ_bankruptcy segfault: its resource_name guarded with idx < resource_count
while its name table holds 19 entries, so it had been reading out of bounds since
resource_count was 23. BL-286 widened it to 31, the overrun grew to 12 slots, and the new
layout put that on unmapped memory. Fixed by guarding on the table extent.

Checking for the same shape elsewhere found ui/presentation.cpp: resource_table is declared
[resource_count], so widening the enum zero-fills the new rows, making resource_name() return
a NULL pointer that every caller passes to "%s". Not reachable today only because callers
guard on a positive quantity and nothing produces the new goods. presentation_of now returns
a placeholder rather than a null. Names and colours for the eight goods stay unauthored,
deliberately - that is design work belonging with BL-287-290 behaviour.

ctest: 40/44 before and after, same four failures (BL-288). No behaviour change beyond the
segfault fix.

BL-288.design:
FOUND BY SWITCHING BUILD DIRECTORIES (2026-08-04), not by a code change. A full ctest run in
build_rel/ (Ninja + Release) reports 4 of 44 failing: ai_skill_harness, data_creep_harness,
settlement_harness, world_audit.

THEY ARE PRE-EXISTING, and that is established rather than assumed. BL-286 extended
resource_type and five ctest failures appeared, so the three BL-286 source files were reverted
to the pre-merge commit and the failing targets rebuilt and re-run. Result: prospective_profit
PASSED pre-merge (that one was a real BL-286 regression, fixed by value-initialising the
resource arrays in components.hpp). These four FAILED pre-merge too. They are not caused by
the resource work.

THE ACTUAL PROBLEM IS THAT NOBODY KNEW. The default build/ directory is configured NMake +
Debug, and that is what every session reaches for. build_rel/ (Ninja + Release) exists and is
not the default. So the Release tier can fail indefinitely without surfacing. At least
settlement_harness passed in Debug at the pre-merge commit while failing in Release at the
same commit — i.e. this is genuine configuration-dependent behaviour, not merely an untested
build.

WHY CONFIGURATION-DEPENDENT FAILURES DESERVE PRIORITY. Debug fills fresh allocations with a
pattern; Release does not. A test that passes only in Debug is usually reading uninitialised
memory or relying on some other undefined behaviour that the optimiser is entitled to change.
The BL-286 NaN was exactly this shape — market_component::price and three siblings had no
initialiser and had been relying on every slot being authored — and it had been latent in the
code waiting for anyone to extend the enum. Four more Release-only failures plausibly hide
more of the same.

WORK. Diagnose each of the four separately; they are unlikely to share one cause. Known
symptom so far: settlement_harness fails "S7d the world-level diversity floor holds across the
corporation set". The others were not diagnosed. Then decide the standing rule — either the
Release tier is green and stays green, or the project states plainly that Debug is the
supported configuration and Release is unsupported. The current position, where Release is
available, faster, and quietly broken, is the worst of the three.

RELATED. BL-287 (verify-tier build time) makes running the full tier cheap enough that this
would have been caught earlier; the two belong in the same batch.
BL-288.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.8). THE PREMISE WAS HALF RIGHT AND THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE FIX. The item said four harnesses fail in Release and nobody noticed because the default tree is Debug. On Linux the canonical tree (build_linux) is now Ninja + RELEASE, so the Debug/Release blindness is already gone here — and a full Release run reported TEN failures, of which exactly ONE was a failing assertion. Each was run alone on an idle machine to find out which: earthlike_lean_trace 121s PASSES, notable_worlds 105s PASSES, mediterranean_sweep 87s PASSES, earthlike_tile_census 58s PASSES (2s under the bound, i.e. passing by luck) — four reported as Timeout purely because every harness carried a flat 60s bound. history_sim_harness and history_sweep did not finish in 400s. econ_stability and home_surface_bench both PASS standalone and failed only because a concurrent build was loading the machine — they assert ABSOLUTE wall-clock times. world_audit fails 1 of 26 assertions, a world-generation finding (BL-291). ai_skill_harness was the single real defect: stale GCC goldens, fixed under BL-285. FIX: three tiers in CMakeLists.txt. Default 60s; IO_TEST_TIMEOUT_LONG raised 120s -> 240s and widened to cover the four measured slow-but-bounded harnesses; a `sweep` label with NO timeout for history_sim_harness/history_sweep, which are open-ended research tools rather than gate tests and are excluded from the routine gate; and a `bench` label on the two wall-clock assertions so a failure there reads as 're-run it idle' rather than as a regression. The documented gate becomes `ctest --test-dir build_linux -LE sweep --output-on-failure` (53 tests). DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md § Merge gate gains the tier table and the reason: a red suite that is mostly noise trains you to ignore it, which is precisely how the one real defect sat unnoticed among nine false positives.

BL-290.design:
FOUND BY THE DOCUMENTATION AUDIT (2026-08-04), reading code against the standing rule added
2026-08-03: "Real history is a mechanism reference, never a name source." The docs passed that
sweep clean. The code did not.

TWO SITES.

1. nation_generation.cpp:577-608 — Pass 5 naming. Two problems, and the second is the worse one.
   (a) The bank is recognisably Latin/European: codas "ia", "us", "is", "or"; onset "Lun"; nouns
   "Republic", "Commonwealth", "Principality", "Protectorate"; adjectives "Free", "United",
   "Sacred". That is trap #1 named in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's own transfers/does-not table —
   "culture-flavoured" must not mean "Earth-culture-flavoured".
   (b) The bank is GLOBAL. It does not read the per-culture phonology that creeds.cpp:64-82
   already rolls, so a nation's gods and the nation's own name come from unrelated sound systems.
   NATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 5 claims the bank is "culture-flavoured"; it is not culture-derived
   at all.

2. city_names.cpp:8-22 — synthetic, but the morphemes are English: "ton", "ford", "haven",
   "burg". Same trap, milder, same fix class.

WHY (b) IS THE INTERESTING HALF. The fix is not "pick less Roman-sounding syllables" — that just
moves the accent. The generator already produces a per-culture phonology upstream; naming should
CONSUME it, so a culture's names, gods and places share one sound system as a consequence of the
chain rather than by coincidence. That is the house pattern (generation as consequence, not dice)
and it makes the Earth-flavour problem structurally impossible rather than merely corrected.

NOT IN SCOPE: body names (Helios, Kepler, Selene, Pallas, Cinder) are Greek/Latin astronomy words,
pre-existing and deliberate — Ben's call if that ever changes.

RELATED: BL-257 (generated body names) is the sibling item on the body axis.
BL-290.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.10). The fix is CONSUMPTION, exactly as the item argued: naming now reads the per-culture phonology the generator already produces, rather than picking less-Roman syllables from a global bank. NEW `src/world/tongue.{hpp,cpp}` lifts the phoneme inventory, the word builder and `coin_lexicon` out of creeds.cpp so downstream passes can consume them; templated on the RNG with an `mt_picker` adapter, so the creeds' splitmix stream and the generation passes' mt19937 share one word-builder. creeds.cpp's own roll is byte-for-byte unchanged (same pick() calls, same order) -- it now RETAINS the tongue on `culture::speech` instead of discarding it. SITE 1 (nation_generation.cpp): the whole Latin/European bank -- k_onsets/k_nuclei/k_codas/k_adjectives/k_nouns -- is DELETED. hard_coded_world.cpp carries each province's tongue into a new `nation_params::seed_tongues`, parallel to the existing seed_tiles anchors; Pass 5 gives each nation the speech of the lowest-indexed seed still inside it after the merge pass and names it in that tongue. SITE 2 (city_names.cpp): the English morpheme bank (ton/ford/haven/burg) is gone. Population centres are placed BEFORE creeds exist, so they are first named from a body-level tongue then re-named by a new `name_population_centres` using the NEAREST province's culture -- the same 'whose gods' rule settlement already uses. NOUNS AND ADJECTIVES WERE GENERATED, NOT DROPPED. Each tongue coins its own words for realm/town/epithet via `coin_lexicon`, which is a PURE FUNCTION OF THE TONGUE -- its stream is seeded by hashing the inventory, not by any caller's RNG. That is what lets nation naming and city naming coin identical morphemes for a culture without sharing a stream or passing words between passes. Dropping the scaffolding would have cost the political map its variety of name SHAPE; this keeps the shape and makes a shared morpheme a visible marker of kinship. SAMPLE (default seed) -- nations: Kemua, Kuamreiteik Tekua, Lu Lakaka, Luthai Muda, Luthai Saikra, Mathkhei Khedath, Ramhihom Zamto, Rerekua Tekua, Ruaruath, Sheldede Shuashua, Tair Memek, Tuavaivuath Vuari, Vuaththi Vuari, Zorzelzo Vuthe. Cities: Damuthrai, Duagual, Hilshesre, Kereimtem, Khualmes, Mitaikri, Shualgual, Thaithairi, Thi Ruari, Tholre Shergual, Vegual, Vushor. THE KINSHIP IS EMERGENT, NOT AUTHORED: Rerekua Tekua / Kuamreiteik Tekua share a realm word; Tuavaivuath Vuari / Vuaththi Vuari likewise; Duagual / Shualgual / Vegual share a settlement morpheme; Luthai Muda / Luthai Saikra share an epithet. That is the house pattern working -- generation as consequence rather than dictionary lookup. DETERMINISM: world_determinism ALL PASS, determinism_harness OK, plus creeds_harness (13), settlement_harness (21), history_ladder_harness and era_world_harness (12). The sample printer was run in two separate processes and diffed identical. All new randomness goes through existing seeded streams or the data-derived tongue hash. TWO DELIBERATE NON-FIXES, both recorded rather than hidden. (1) creeds.cpp's DOMAINS and EPITHETS ('the sea', 'who counts the spears') stay English BY DESIGN -- the header states the common-trade-tongue rule, so prose goes common while proper names stay native. A deliberate exemption, not an oversight. (2) The PHONEME POOLS themselves are unchanged and lean faintly Semitic/Polynesian in aggregate; no single culture reads that way because per-culture subsetting scatters it, and changing the pool would alter every creed name in every existing world. The item scoped the fix to consumption, not the inventory. THIRD SITE FOUND, NOT IN THE ITEM: `region_word` in settlement.cpp -- province names are '<culture> <region word>' with an English region word (Reach, Coast). Same fault class and now the most visible remaining one, since the province list reads half-native half-English. Filed as BL-348.

BL-291.design:
FOUND BY THE DOCUMENTATION AUDIT (2026-08-04). world_audit is one of the four harnesses BL-288
(Release-only test failures) records as failing, but it carries a consequence the others do not:
it is the harness that PRODUCED the measured landform distribution table in TILES.md § Measured
landform distribution.

THE KNOCK-ON. Two commits on 2026-08-04 moved relief on every generated world — 802421c took
mountain+highland 6.8% -> 17.5%, then 71e8a9b (convergent-boundary seeding) settled it at 14.0%,
with seeds 7/6/3 -> 13/11/5. The documented table is therefore stale, and cannot be regenerated
until this harness runs. Stale MEASURED numbers are worse than absent ones, because they read as
verified.

SO THE ITEM IS TWO STEPS, in order: fix the harness, then re-run it and re-issue the table. The
doc has been marked stale-and-blocked in the meantime, pointing here.

RELATION TO BL-288: same failure set, but BL-288 is about the Debug/Release gap that hid four
failures. This one is about the specific instrument and the doc it feeds. Fixing BL-288's build
question does not by itself re-issue the census.

## Worked 2026-08-07 — the premise was wrong

**world_audit is not broken.** It configures, builds (`cmake --build build --target world_audit`) and runs to completion, printing the full landform census this item said could not be produced. It exits non-zero because ONE assertion fails — S2's biome-balance check — out of 26. The 'harness fails' framing came from reading a non-zero exit as a broken instrument, and it cost the doc three days of a stale-and-blocked banner for no reason.

**Step 2 is therefore done, and step 1 was never needed.** TILES.md's measured landform table is re-issued from today's run, with land-tile counts and a note that the earlier '~14.0% relief' figure was a home-body number quoted as a system one (actual: 12.1% system, 15.3% Kepler). Kepler's 0.0% valley survived re-measurement — it is real, not a stale artifact.

**What remains is not this item's.** The S2 failure is a world-generation finding: forest+wetland 2.41% against a 3% target, with wetland at 12 tiles (0.08%) on the whole home body. Two tangled questions — is that a regression from the 2026-08-04 relief commits, and is an ocean-inclusive denominator right for a land-only biome — both Ben's call. Filed as a review entry rather than retuned to green.

**Check BL-288's other three.** This item was one of four harnesses BL-288 records as failing. If 'failing' was inferred from exit codes there too, the other three deserve the same look before anyone budgets repair work for them.
BL-291.resolution: Closed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.8). Substantively resolved 2026-08-07, when the premise was found to be wrong — world_audit was never broken; it configures, builds, runs to completion and prints the full landform census, exiting non-zero because ONE assertion of 26 fails (S2 biome balance). Re-verified at the cut: still exactly 1/26, and the census re-issued into TILES.md § Measured landform distribution stands. The last residual thread closed here: TILES.md carried a 2026-08-04 note saying Kepler's 0.0% valley 'needs re-measuring' after Pass 5's ring->landform rewrite. BL-293.design:
FOUND BY THE DOCUMENTATION AUDIT (2026-08-04), and independently logged in Project-Rival's own
findings doc as its ranked gap #4 — so this is the second time it has surfaced.

THE GAP. `ACTIONS.json` carries gameplay entries for `place_sell_order`, `remove_sell_order` and
`set_workforce_auto`. None has a `corp_verb`; the enum in corp_command.hpp is eight wide and holds
none of them. So they are player-only presses: a text-driven player can READ the order book and
can be told what the press MEANS, but has no way to issue it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THREE MISSING VERBS. Standing sell orders with a floor price are how a
corporation governs the release of its own stock rather than dumping at the resolved price
(SYSTEMS.md § Trade). An agent that cannot place one is not playing the economy; it is watching
it. The word interface is v0.1.1's theme and this is the hole in its write leg.

ALSO FIX THE OVERCLAIM: ACTIONS.md's preamble says pairing the three legs gives an LLM "the full
word interface". Until this lands that is false, and it is the one line in the dictionary most
likely to mislead. Either close the gap or state the narrowing — closing it is better.

SEQUENCING: the gameplay family is TRANSCRIBED from corp_command.hpp, never authored. So the seam
changes first, then the dictionary is re-transcribed and the mirror re-rendered.

## Scope correction 2026-08-07 — stopped before coding

The item assumes the three presses only lack a verb. They lack a PLACE TO PUT ONE. `sell_order` is defined in world/components.hpp:368 but stored in ui_state.hpp:273 and handed to `clear_markets` by the caller (app.cpp:566); the world has no order book. A corp_verb mutates `world&`, so there is nothing to mutate.

Also found: no serialisation path touches sell_order or buy_order, so standing orders appear not to survive save/load — a defect independent of this item.

And the gate: corp_verb is the seam corp_ai.cpp drives every rival corp through. The standing rules enumerate what that scored-utility layer may do and TRADING IS NOT ON THE LIST. Adding place_sell_order widens the AI's reach as a side effect. That is Ben's call, so this stopped at the finding. See the review entry for the three options.

Difficulty and files as filed are both understated: this is Full-mode, save-format-touching work, not a transcription follow-up.
BL-293.resolution:
LANDED 2026-08-08, at the size the 2026-08-07 scope correction found rather than the size it was filed at.

Ben's ruling (NR-083): "Order book needs to be a background process, the AI must be able to trade as a player does."
The player-only fence proposed alongside it was explicitly rejected.

WHAT LANDED.
1. The order book is world state. `world::sell_orders` / `buy_orders` / `next_order_id`; orders carry a stable
   `id` so removal names identity rather than an index. It lived on ui_state, which cost three things at once:
   clearing was UI-driven, a corp_verb had nothing to mutate, and standing orders were outside the save seam.
2. It is serialised. `order_book.{hpp,cpp}` - magic IOOB + version, the second flat-binary stream in world/*
   after history_log, refusing a bad stream rather than reinterpreting it.
3. Matching is a background process. `clear_markets` DROPPED both order-list parameters and reads the world;
   a headless tick now sells a standing order with nobody handing it over.
4. Three verbs joined the seam: place_sell_order, remove_sell_order, set_workforce_auto (enum now 11 wide,
   append-only). The Market Ledger's buttons queue corp_commands that app::render applies through
   apply_corp_command - the player's press and the AI's command are one implementation, not two that agree.
5. Rival corps trade, per the ruling. Conservative first cut: surplus past a hold threshold, half the excess,
   floored at the market's rarity price, scored at the floor. Tunables in corp_ai_params. See NR-087.
6. The standing rules were amended - the rival-corp exception's verb list did not include trading, and Ben's
   ruling widens it. Flagged explicitly rather than slipped in: NR-085.

FOUND ALONG THE WAY. `set_workforce` never cleared `workforce_auto`, though ACTIONS.json has always said it did
and the UI has always done it - so a command-driven agent's target was silently re-solved on the next tick. The
seam now matches the press (NR-086). `state_hash` was also missing `workforce_auto` (NR-088).

REVIEW FOUND A VALUE-MINTING BUG. Overlapping sell orders on one (corp, body, resource) were each listed against the
FULL pool and each debited it: a pool of 10 with two orders of 10 ended at -10 units with the corp paid for 20. Plus
the mirror under-sell in the auto-clear pass. Pre-existing and UI-reachable, but this item is what made it reachable
by a scorer in a loop, so it was fixed here (NR-092) and is now covered by order_book_harness R1b.

VERIFICATION. `order_book_harness` 45/45 PASS, including the determinism assertion the move earns: the same
orders in a different SEQUENCE hash differently, because matching is price-TIME priority and the book's order is
state. econ/corp_ai/corp_agency/history_log/econ_stability/corp_ai_predictive all green. ai_skill_harness's
net-worth golden bands fail - but they already failed 5 assertions at unmodified HEAD, and every determinism
assertion passes on both sides; not re-blessed (NR-090). The one visual requirement is unverified because the
app does not build at HEAD for an unrelated pre-existing reason (NR-091). data_creep_harness R1 passes at HEAD and
fails here - rival trading delays the build plateau from tick 500 to tick 1000, still flat to 1500; not re-blessed
(NR-093).

DICTIONARY. Sequenced last, as required: the seam changed first, then ACTIONS.json was re-transcribed from
corp_command.hpp and the mirror re-rendered. The 'full word interface' overclaim turned out to live in
render_actions.js's hardcoded preamble as well as in _note; both corrected, and the replacement states what is
still NOT reachable (the buy side has a save format but no verb) rather than making a fresh sweeping claim.
